out.text: Not right yet: the purple 2x4 is horizontal, wider than it is tall. It touches the right side of the red slope, and its bottom lines up with the slope's bottom. It needs to stand vertically, 2 studs wide and 4 tall, so its top is one stud above the slope's top.
Yes, the purple 2x4 is vertical and touches the right side of the red slope. Its bottom lines up with the slope's bottom, and its top sticks out one stud above the slope's top.

Not yet. The photo shows only the red slope and the purple brick on the plate. There is no lime green brick to the right of the purple one. The wearer is holding something small and light-colored in their right hand, off the plate.

Not right yet: the lime brick is vertical and touches the right side of the purple brick. But it's level with the purple brick's top, and its bottom lines up with the purple brick's bottom. It needs to be one stud higher, so it sticks out one stud above the purple brick.

Not confirmed yet, because the placement doesn't match the step.

The lime brick is vertical and touches the right side of the purple brick at its top. Its top looks to be about one stud above the purple brick's top, but I can't judge that with certainty.

The red slope is touching the left edge of the plate, but the purple brick looks to be about one stud above the slope's top. The lime brick is directly beside the purple brick's top edge.

Looking closer, the lime brick's top sits slightly above the purple's top, and the lime appears to be 2 studs tall. That looks about right. I can't tell for sure whether it extends exactly one stud above the purple brick, because the photo is taken at an angle and the brick is small.

Please bring the plate closer and hold it still so I can check.

Not confirmed: the brick right of the purple one is beige/tan, not pure white. It is horizontal, 6 studs long, and its left end touches the purple brick just below the lime exhaust. A pure white one-by-six has to replace it.

Not quite. The white one-by-six is horizontal, 6 studs long, and its left end touches the purple brick. But it sits level with the purple brick's second stud from the top, not "just below the lime exhaust". The lime brick is above the purple brick's top-left corner, so it looks like the white brick is one row lower than the exhaust. I can't be sure the white is pure white rather than cream.

I'm not confirming the step. The white brick needs to touch the purple brick and sit directly below the lime exhaust's row.

Not yet. The white one-by-four isn't on the plate. The body ends at the right with the two white bricks and the lime brick, and nothing is against that right end. The wearer is holding a small white piece in their right hand, but it isn't placed.

Not right yet: the right wheel is too far below the body. There is a gap of empty studs between its top and the blue and lime bricks, so it doesn't touch them. It also sits mostly under the lime brick and the white end brick, and it should sit under the right part of the blue brick and the left part of the lime brick.

Not confirmed yet: the right wheel is too far from the body. Its top doesn't reach the blue and lime bricks, and a gap of plate shows between them.

The disc sits below the blue brick, roughly under its left-middle part, and it doesn't touch the lime brick. It needs to move up against the body, under the right part of the blue brick and the left part of the lime brick. The area below the white 1x4 at the right end is bare, which is correct.

Not confirmed yet: the yellow one-by-four is in the ground row and touches the right end of the white ground brick. But the plate extends several studs past its right end, so the row doesn't reach the right edge. The yellow brick should sit flush with the plate's right edge.
You're holding the purple two-by-four in your right hand. It's lying flat, just right of the plate and not on it yet. The red slope is still the only brick on the plate.
There are three red pieces on the plate. They are the red slope at the left edge and the two red round discs below the body, which are the wheels.

Yes, the two red discs look about the same size, each roughly four studs across. The left one sits below the red slope at the left edge of the plate. The right one sits below the blue and lime bricks.

Not right yet: the purple 2x4 is lying horizontally (wider than tall) right of the red slope. It needs to stand vertically, 2 studs wide and 4 tall, with its top one stud above the red slope's top. It does touch the slope's right side, and its bottom is level with the slope's bottom.

Step 2 looks right. The purple 2x4 is vertical, 2 studs wide and 4 tall, and touches the right side of the red slope. Its bottom is level with the slope's bottom, and its top sticks out one stud above the slope.

Not yet: I can only see the red slope and the purple brick on the plate. There's no lime green brick to the right of the purple one. The wearer's right hand is holding a small piece above the table, and the loose lime bricks are still lying next to the plate.

Not right yet. The lime brick is vertical and touches the right side of the purple brick. But its top is level with the purple brick's top, and it needs to stick out one stud above it. Its bottom also lines up with the purple brick's bottom, so it needs to sit one stud higher.

Not confirmed yet. The lime brick is vertical and touches the right side of the purple brick at its top, but I can't tell if its top is exactly one stud above the purple's top. In the photo it looks about level with the purple's top or only slightly above it, so it may need to be raised one stud.

Not confirmed: the brick right of the purple one is beige or tan, not pure white. It is horizontal, six studs long, and its left end touches the purple brick just below the lime exhaust. The tan brick should be swapped for a pure white one-by-six.

Not right yet. The white one-by-six is horizontal and its left end touches the purple brick, but it sits level with the purple brick's second row from the top. It also looks cream or off-white. The lime exhaust is above it and is not touching the white brick's row.

Not yet: I can't see a white one-by-four against the right end of the body. The white bricks end in a straight edge, and the lime brick below them is level with that edge, but nothing stands vertically at that end. The wearer holds a small white piece in their right hand, and a white one-by-four lies loose on the table above the plate.

Not right yet: the right wheel is not touching the body. A row of empty studs separates it from the blue and lime bricks, and its top sits below them. It needs to move up so its top touches the right part of the blue brick and the left part of the lime brick.

The left wheel and the right wheel look about 3 columns apart, which seems fine. The plate is bare below the white 1x4 at the right end.

I can't confirm step 10 from this photo. The right wheel is below the body, but it looks too far from the body and too far left.

The disc's top looks like it sits slightly below the blue and lime bricks. There seems to be a small gap, so I can't see it touching them. Its right edge is around the lime brick's right end, which is further left than the white 1x4. Bare plate does show below the white 1x4, which is correct.

The gap between the two discs looks like about three columns, but the plate is photographed at an angle, so I can't count the studs reliably.

The disc should touch the underside of the right part of the blue brick and the left part of the lime brick. It may need to move up against them.

Not confirmed yet: the yellow brick is in the ground row and touches the right end of the white ground brick, but it doesn't reach the right edge of the plate. The plate's right edge is at about x=600 at that row, so the yellow brick looks flush with it, or maybe a stud short. Looking closer, the plate's green area shows about 2–3 empty studs to its right, around x=610 and beyond. I can't say for sure.
You're holding the purple two-by-four in your right hand. It's lying flat and horizontal, just right of the plate, and it isn't on the plate yet. The red slope is still the only brick on the plate.
There are three red pieces on the plate. They are the red slope at the left edge and the two round red discs below the body, which are the left and right wheels.

Yes, the two red discs look about the same size. Both are round, red, and roughly four studs across. The left one is at the left edge of the plate, below the red slope. The right one is below the blue and lime bricks.

The red slope is horizontal, red, and flush against the left edge of the plate. There are empty studs above it (about five rows) and below it (several rows), so it touches neither the top nor the bottom edge.

Not right yet: the purple 2x4 is lying horizontally, wider than it is tall, and it sits directly right of the red slope. Its top is level with the slope's top, not one stud above it. It needs to stand vertically, with its bottom level with the slope's bottom.
Yes, the purple 2x4 is vertical and touches the right side of the red slope. Its bottom is level with the slope's bottom, and its top sticks out one stud above the slope.

Not yet: the plate shows only the red brick and the purple vertical brick. I don't see a lime brick right of the purple one. The wearer's right hand is holding a small piece above the plate, and it isn't placed.

Not right yet: the lime brick is vertical and touches the right side of the purple brick, but it isn't one stud above the purple brick's top. Its top looks level with the purple top, and its bottom is level with the purple bottom, so it reaches down to the red slope's bottom row. It needs to sit one stud higher, sticking out above the purple brick.

Not confirmed yet. Judging by the photo, the lime brick is vertical and touches the right side of the purple brick, but it sits too high.

The purple brick is vertical, and its top is about one stud above the red slope. The lime brick is at the purple brick's top corner. Its top looks level with, or only slightly above, the purple top, not a full stud above. Its bottom seems to reach about the second stud down on the purple brick. The lime brick should stick out one stud above the purple top, so it probably needs to sit one stud lower.

No, the step isn't right yet. The brick right of the purple one is beige or tan, not pure white. It is horizontal, 6 studs long, and its left end touches the purple brick just below the lime exhaust. The white one-by-six needs to replace it, and the tan one should be kept for the ground row later.

Not quite. The white one-by-six is horizontal and its left end touches the purple brick, but it sits level with the purple brick's second stud from the top. It isn't directly below the lime exhaust, and a stud gap shows between them.

The white brick looks pure white and about six studs long. I'm not confident about the exact row alignment from this angle, so I'm not confirming the step.

Not yet: the white one-by-four isn't on the plate. The body is built up to the lime brick at the right end of the bottom row, and nothing stands against the right ends of the white bricks and the lime brick. A small white piece is in the wearer's right hand, off the plate.

Not right yet: the right wheel isn't touching the body. There is a gap of about one row of empty studs between the disc's top and the blue and lime bricks. It needs to move up so its top touches the right part of the blue brick and the left part of the lime brick.

The wheel's position left and right looks about correct. The plate below the white brick at the right end is bare.

Not confirmed yet: the right red disc doesn't touch the body, and the empty-column count doesn't match.

The disc sits clearly below the blue and lime bricks. A gap of bare plate, about one row of studs, separates its top from them. It needs to move up until it touches the right part of the blue brick and the left part of the lime brick.

The left wheel is also separated from the red slope by a gap. I can't judge the three-column spacing until the disc is moved.

The plate below the white 1x4 at the right end is bare, which is correct.

Not yet: the yellow one-by-four is in the ground row and touches the right end of the white ground brick, but its right end stops short of the plate's right edge. The plate shows about one stud of green to its right, so it needs to move or sit one stud further right to reach the edge.
You're holding the purple two-by-four in your right hand. It's lying flat, just off the right edge of the plate, and it isn't on the plate yet.
There are three red pieces on the plate. They are the red slope at the left edge of the body and the two red round discs, which are the wheels below the body.

Yes, the two red discs look about the same size. Both are round and roughly four studs across. The left one is below the red slope at the left edge, and the right one is below the blue and lime bricks.
